models._note:
Identity, limits, pricing, endpoints, and request-shape constraints: OpenAI model page and changelog, retrieved 2026-09-08 (BST-1692):
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog
1,050,000 total context with a 922K maximum input.
ENDPOINT: the changelog says tool calling requires the Responses API. The direct `openai` route builds the default `createOpenAI()(modelId)` callable, which @ai-sdk/openai 4.0.49 resolves to its Responses model (POST /responses), so tool calling is available on the surface we use (packages/agent/src/providers/provider-factory.ts, `case 'openai'`).
CACHE RATES OMITTED: OpenAI publishes $1/MTok cached input and $12.50/MTok cache writes, but a cache RATE may only travel with a `promptCaching` dialect (BST-1354, provider-registry-pricing.test.ts) and that enum has no `openai` member. Recording the rates without a dialect would price a discount the runtime never requests. Every sibling OpenAI row omits them for the same reason; adding an OpenAI caching dialect is separate work.
LONG-CONTEXT SURCHARGE NOT MODELLED: OpenAI bills prompts above 272K input tokens at 2x input/cache and 1.5x output. computeCost in packages/tokenization/src/cost-estimate.ts applies one flat rate per token class and models no per-request tier, so estimates for prompts over 272K input tokens UNDERSTATE the real charge. The catalog schema has no tier field, and the same gap covers gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna, which share this 1,050,000 context window; adding a tier is BST-1708. Pricing is NOT omitted to dodge it: an unpriced row reports no cost for EVERY request, which is a larger and far more common misstatement than understating the rare >272K one.
REASONING LADDER DECLARED: the model page lists effort low/medium/high/xhigh/max with no `none` rung. This is the first DIRECT `openai` row to carry a `reasoning` block, because the undeclared fallback (OPENAI_FAMILY_DEFAULT_EFFORTS in packages/assistant-contract/src/model-reasoning.ts) is wrong for Astra in both directions: it offers `minimal`, which the page does not list, and withholds `max`, which it does. The 12 sibling openai rows still inherit that fallback (BST-1709). `mandatory` is false: effort is optional, and leaving it unset is the composer's Auto.
The model accepts no custom temperature or top_p.
models.label: GPT-6 Astra

_note:
OpenRouter uses provider-prefixed model slugs (examples in docs):
https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/auto-model-selection
Curated current subset from OpenRouter's model catalog. Provider-reported
billed cost is authoritative at runtime; these rates are display estimates.
PRICING SOURCE RULE (BST-1705): every rate in this block is the STANDARD
route's BASE rate, re-verified against the live Models API on 2026-09-10.
Two things in that API will hand you a different number if you read it
naively, and both have already corrupted rows here:
1. `pricing.overrides` — an array of bands that REPLACE the base rate.
   `utc_days`/`utc_start`/`utc_end` bands are time-of-day surge pricing, so
   `pricing.prompt` inside a peak window is the rate RIGHT NOW, not the
   standing price (this is how tencent/hy3 was recorded at its 1.6x surge).
   `min_prompt_tokens` bands are long-context tiers (BST-1708), carried on
   the row as `pricing.longContextTiers` with the BASE rate left in
   `inputPerMTok`/`outputPerMTok`. Record the base: on a banded route
   that is THE CHEAPEST BAND. Not "the rate outside every band" (bands
   that leave part of the week uncovered are rejected, so there is no
   outside) and not the band covering most of the week (hy3 surges 16
   hours in 24, so its modal band IS the surge). Known limit: a
   promotional band under the standing rate would read as the base;
   nothing live does that as of 2026-09-10.
2. Variant routes — `<id>:batch`, `:free`, `:nitro`. A variant is a
   DIFFERENT route with its own price and belongs in a row of its own if we
   ever ship one; its rate must never occupy the standard route's row (this
   is how google/gemini-3.7-flash and z-ai/glm-5.3-flash were recorded).
LIMIT RULE (BST-1804): contextWindow / maxOutputTokens are the route's
`top_provider` pair, never a larger model-level `context_length` (used only
where the top-provider window is null, i.e. router meta-models).
All three rules are mechanised in scripts/openrouter-pricing-audit.mjs — run
`pnpm run audit:openrouter-pricing` when adding, re-pricing or re-limiting a row.

models._note:
These are the RUNTIME budgets, not Gemma 4 E2B's architectural limits
(the model spec lists ~128K context). The local provider runs q4f16
weights through transformers.js on WebGPU, where prefilling a large
prompt allocates an O(seq^2) attention buffer that exhausts GPU memory
and aborts ONNX Runtime (SafeInt overflow / std::bad_alloc) well below
the architectural window — empirically in the low thousands of tokens
on a typical device. Declaring 131_072/8192 told the context-budget
machinery (deriveEffectiveInputBudget -> agentLoop.inputTokenLimit ->
Mastra TokenLimiter) and the meter that ~128K was usable, so multi-turn
and tool-calling contexts ballooned straight into an OOM crash. These
conservative values keep the assembled prompt bounded and cap local
generation; a prompt that still exceeds a given device's GPU is caught
by the engine-fault reset in llm-host-runtime (recovers + reports
instead of poisoning the session). NOTE: this is RUNTIME-only metadata
(no DB model-catalog migration). The DB catalog row (migration
028-gemma-local-llm.ts) still carries the DESCRIPTIVE
capabilities.contextWindow: 131072, which is intentionally NOT
consulted for budgeting — this static registry value is the sole
budget source for the built-in 'local' provider — so the two
diverging is harmless, not a bug. The deeper fix for reliable local
tool-calling is a leaner local system-prompt/tool-schema footprint.
models.label: Gemma 4 E2B
